_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. The factory regen for this connector lives in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/threatdown (tooling/derive_spec.py builds the derived spec, tooling/apply_handfixes.py re-applies the generated-file edits).

handfixes.summary: The client-credentials token mint builds its default scope from a list (execute, read, write) joined with spaces, in both the client auto-mint and `auth login`. The wire value is unchanged: scope=execute read write. THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE still overrides it, split on whitespace.
handfixes.why: Press dogfood's oauth_scope_coverage scan reads the generated single string "execute read write" as one scope and reported 0/418 operations covered, failing shipcheck on a correct CLI. The list form lets the scan see each scope. Recorded by the build pane in .printing-press-patches/oauth-scope-list.json and re-applied after a cross-spec regenerate by cli-factory/threatdown/tooling/apply_handfixes.py; a reprint that skips that script reverts to resolveClientCredentialsScope() while go build and go test stay green.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a press fix to the scope-coverage scan (split space-delimited scope literals); no spec extension can express it.

handfixes.summary: The root command's Short and Long help open with "ThreatDown OneView CLI" instead of the generated "Threatdown CLI".
handfixes.why: The press title-cases the API slug (threatdown -> Threatdown), which miscases the vendor brand on the first line of `threatdown-cli --help` and in the agent-context description. Applied at msp-skills onboarding (2026-10-14) to the stripped source; cli-factory/threatdown/tooling/apply_handfixes.py does not carry it, so a reprint reverts it unless this entry catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The derived spec already sets x-display-name "ThreatDown OneView"; the press should use it for the root help line instead of title-casing the slug.

handfixes.summary: Generated SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and guide.md (the source README) carry corrections for this CLI: the teach example passes --resource-type, the Claude Code MCP registration passes both OAuth env vars, the async-jobs section explains `respond --wait`, the respond verbs are documented as preview-until---confirm, and guide.md documents THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE and the client-secret prompt. SKILL.md and guide.md say the CLI requests a new token when the client or THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE changes and refuses to borrow another client's token (round 5, 2026-10-14), and SKILL.md's read-only line names endpoints diag-log.
handfixes.why: These files are re-rendered on every generate and re-vendored by onboard.py on every --resume. The generated text was wrong for this CLI: teach without --resource-type fails, `claude mcp add` with no --env gives an MCP server that 401s, and the generic `--dry-run` wording implied a preview the respond verbs do not give. Applied by cli-factory/threatdown/tooling/apply_handfixes.py (DOC_EDITS); a reprint that skips it ships the wrong instructions while every build gate stays green.

handfixes.summary: The respond verbs (isolate, restore, scan, reboot, update) print a target preview and send nothing without --confirm or the global --yes, and refuse more than --max-targets endpoints (default 25).
handfixes.why: This is the safety property governance.md, page.json and the README promise for the only commands that act on client machines by host name. The code is hand-written (respond_isolate.go is a novel file regen-merge keeps), but a reprint that regenerated the respond scaffold, or a refactor that flipped the default, would send jobs on a bare `respond isolate --host X` while the docs still say it previews. The asserts pin the preview note, the default cap and the refusal.

handfixes.summary: Secret-named JSON keys (as_uninstall_password, uninstall_password, password, secret, secret_hash, secret_token, token, custom_headers) are dropped at any depth before any row reaches the local store (generic blob, typed columns and FTS index, via the single mergeIncomingResourceData choke point), and an HTTP response that carries one is never written to the response cache. Helper: internal/cliutil/secretfields.go. The installers response (account-specific download links and signed URLs, no secret-named key) is also never cached (cliutil.IsSecretBearingPath) and never stored (mergeIncomingResourceData stores an empty object for the installers resource).
handfixes.why: Default `sync` pulls GET /v1/policies, whose every row carries as_uninstall_password (the tamper-protection password that uninstalls the ThreatDown agent), and GET /v1/notifications/subscriptions, whose rows carry the HMAC signing key secret_token; the generated store wrote both into data.db and resources_fts, and the response cache wrote GET bodies such as /v1/policies/{id}/secret to disk. Found at msp-skills onboarding (2026-10-14) by scanning the spec's 2xx response schemas for password/secret/token keys. A reprint regenerates store.go and client.go and silently drops both hooks while go build and go test stay green. internal/store/secret_fields_test.go proves both directions: with the hook reverted the sentinel lands in resources_fts. custom_headers was added after the round-1 adversarial review drove a webhook subscription whose custom_headers carried 'authorization: Bearer <sentinel>' into data.db, resources_fts and the response cache (the spec's example header key is authorization). installers was added after the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-14) found `installers <account_id>` writing its signed url and link into the HTTP response cache while governance.md tiers it as credential-bearing; secret_fields_test.go upserts an installers row with a sentinel and fails with the guard reverted.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a press feature: an x-secret / writeOnly-aware store projection that never persists credential fields; no spec extension expresses it today.

handfixes.summary: governance.md, README.md and page.json put every read whose output carries a credential in the Credential tier, not Read: every policies read (list/get/search/system-default/-v2/secret-get), sites secret, installation-tokens search, installers, webhooks and notifications list / get, and export of policies or notifications (export has no webhooks resource). governance.md also names the MCP read-only mode's GET gap. `export` is not listed as a blanket Read command.
handfixes.why: The generated governance tiers by verb, so 'every list / get / search' was Read and an agent policy keyed on it would let an agent read every customer's tamper-protection password. Applied at msp-skills onboarding (2026-10-14); these files are preserved across onboard --resume but a fleet re-mint or a hand rewrite can drop the carve-out. Round-2 review (2026-10-14) found `export policies` / `export notifications` dumping uninstall passwords and signing keys while `export` was named in the Read row. Round-3 review (2026-10-14) found `export` cannot export webhooks, so the wording names policies and notifications only.

handfixes.summary: Every variable the binaries read is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb user_config + server.mcp_config.env), server.json (MCP Registry) and the three mcp-install.md env blocks. Beyond the client id and secret these are the optional THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE, THREATDOWN_BASE_URL, THREATDOWN_TOKEN_URL, THREATDOWN_USER_AGENT, THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY, THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, blank (not placeholders) in mcp-install.md.
handfixes.why: check_env_schema failed the onboard with 7 read-but-undeclared variables, so a Claude Desktop install could never set read-only mode or a reduced scope. onboard.py --resume re-vendors manifest.json from the press source, which declares only the two credentials, so a re-onboard drops the other seven while the build stays green (check_env_schema would then catch it; this entry names the cause). Applied at msp-skills onboarding 2026-10-14. 2026-10-22: the read-only switch is preset to "1" in every mcp-install.md config block by the interim security note. 2026-11-02 (press 4.35.1 reprint): THREATDOWN_NO_LOCAL_DATA (new in 4.34) declared on all three channels.

handfixes.summary: Every documented `threatdown-mcp --transport http` launch (README ChatGPT line and FAQ, mcp-install.md remote section) sets THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and says callers send it as Authorization: Bearer.
handfixes.why: The scaffolded docs launched `threatdown-mcp --transport http` with only the OAuth credentials; the binary exits 1 with 'THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN must be set to a non-empty bearer token before starting --transport http' (measured 2026-10-14), so the documented ChatGPT/remote path never started. check_install_docs does not check the token, so nothing gates this. 2026-10-22 (follow-up to #428): the README.md / page.json remote-agent (HTTP mode) prose this entry guarded was removed on purpose when the interim security note paused HTTP mode until the reprint; restore those markers with the post-reprint docs fix. 2026-11-02 (press 4.35.1 reprint): the interim note is retired; the README ChatGPT line and FAQ are restored with the 4.35.1 HTTP mode (token of at least 32 characters, loopback unless TLS) and the mcp-install.md launch exports the token on its own line.

handfixes.summary: doctor reports an ERROR api verdict (and an ERROR credentials verdict) when the OneView account probe GET /v1/info/account returns 404, instead of 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)' and a WARN.
handfixes.why: check_doctor_truth (CI hard gate, issue #282) failed the onboard: a THREATDOWN_BASE_URL that is not the OneView API root made doctor report the API as healthy. Generated doctor.go has no doctorUnexpectedStatus/doctorWrongBaseURL (the fleet's hand-wired fix), so a reprint reverts this; the gate would then fail again. Applied at msp-skills onboarding 2026-10-14.

handfixes.summary: An env-sourced THREATDOWN_BASE_URL or THREATDOWN_TOKEN_URL is marked as an env override in config.Load and configForSave writes the file's own value back instead, so config.toml never captures the override and unsetting the variable restores the default on the next run.
handfixes.why: The generated configForSave restored only env-sourced ClientID/ClientSecret, so the first token mint (auth login, doctor or any MCP tool call) wrote the env base_url and token_url into config.toml. After that, unsetting the variable had no effect: requests kept going to the old base URL and every new mint sent the client ID and secret to the old token host. The doctor hint ('or unset it'), the manifest's 'leave blank for the default' and governance.md's 'override' were all false after one use. Found by the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-14); a reprint regenerates config.go and silently reverts it while go build and go test stay green. internal/config/env_urls_test.go fails with the restore lines removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect (66 of 68 fleet configs behave the same): configForSave should restore every env-overridden field, not only credentials.

handfixes.summary: governance.md's tier tables name every non-GET write command in the binary (job issue and cancel, policy -v2 writes, group assignment, alert routing, email-protection, imports, every delete) plus endpoints diag-log, and state the rule for anything missing: a POST, PUT or DELETE pp:method that is not a search, export or report query is Security config at minimum. README.md and page.json carry the same Endpoint actions list.
handfixes.why: The generated governance tiers by keyword, and the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-14) enumerated 310 non-GET commands from agent-context and found dozens in no tier (notifications change-owner / remove-email can silence alerting; groups assign-endpoints moves machines across policies). governance.md is preserved across onboard --resume, but a fleet re-mint or a hand rewrite can shrink the tables back to examples.

handfixes.summary: A client-credentials token is saved with token_binding, a fingerprint of the client ID, scope and token URL it was minted for (config.TokenBindingFor). tokenBoundElsewhere is true when the current process's client ID, THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE or token URL give a different fingerprint, or the token is unbound (auth set-token) while client credentials are configured; then the client mints its own token, and when it has no secret to mint with, authHeader returns an error instead of the cached token. validateCachedRequestAuth resolves the token first so a response cached under another client's token is never served. resolveClientCredentials trims like auth login. auth login records the binding, auth set-token clears it. Round 6 (2026-10-14): the refusal is the typed client.ErrTokenBoundElsewhere, which exits with the auth code 4 and which doctor reports as a credentials error (the API is not probed); an unbound token yields to a client ID or a secret (either one); and config.Load never pairs an environment client ID with the secret saved for a different client in credentials.toml. Round 7 (2026-10-14): auth login given either flag saves the exact client pair it minted with, and save() keeps the saved pair in its snapshot so a second mint in one process (tail --follow, a long sync) does not write it back empty. A hand-written auth_header counts as an unbound token (it yields to a configured client ID or secret), and a [headers] Authorization entry is never sent: auth comes only from the bound token path.
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). Every process run as the same OS user shares one credentials.toml, and the generated needsClientCredentialsMint checked only token presence and expiry. So an MCP server configured with a separate read-only OAuth client (and THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE=read) reused the admin's cached execute token and issued an isolation job through threatdown_execute, with no token request of its own; the README's 'the CLI can only do what that client is permitted to do' was false. A reprint regenerates client.go, config.go, credentials.go and auth.go and silently reverts this while go build and go test stay green. Round 5 (adversarial + Codex, 2026-10-14) found the first version failed open: a process with a client ID but no secret, or only THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE set, still used the admin token; a GET cache hit (keyed on the cached token) served the other client's data before authHeader ran; and an unbound token outranked configured credentials. internal/client/token_binding_test.go (both tests) fails with any of these guards removed. Codex review round 6 (2026-10-14), two P1s: AuthHeader() sends auth_header ahead of any token, and the configured-header loop overwrote the bound Authorization, so a saved admin bearer in either place rode a reporting client or a narrower scope. TestHandWrittenAuthHeaderYieldsToClient and TestConfiguredHeadersNeverCarryAuthorization fail on revert. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): the credentials literal gained BaseURL and RefreshLoginID (assert re-aligned), and the 4.35.1 logout path clears refreshLoginID/refreshLoginKeep, so the binding clear sits after them.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: the press's client-credentials cache should key the token on the client ID and scope.

handfixes.summary: endpoints diag-log (a GET that makes the endpoint generate a diagnostic log) is NeedsConfirm and Mutating in the MCP code-orchestration table, so threatdown_read refuses it, threatdown_execute previews it until confirm is boolean true, and THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 refuses it; the CLI command no longer carries mcp:read-only; its signed download URL is never written to the HTTP response cache (IsSecretBearingPath); the CLI sends it through GetMutating (never cached, never retried) behind the --data-source gate.
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). The generated read-only gate allowed every GET, so a 'reporting agent' MCP server could make client endpoints generate logs, which governance.md tiers as an Endpoint action. The response is a signed S3 URL that was cached at rest and served on a repeat call without asking the endpoint again. code_orch.go, endpoints_diag-log.go and secretfields' caller are regenerated on a reprint; TestCodeOrchExecuteReadOnlyRefusesNonGET in code_orch_writebody_test.go fails if diag-log stops being refused. Codex review round 5 (2026-10-14): the CLI still sent it through the read path, so a dropped response replayed the request (TestDiagLogIsNeverRetried: 4 API hits before, 1 after). Review round 10: the first GetMutating cut skipped validateDataSourceStrategy, so --data-source local fired the action live. TestDiagLogRefusesLocalDataSource. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): press 4.35.1 gates Mutating and NeedsConfirm endpoints natively (read/execute split, confirm preview, read-only refusal), so the hand-written codeOrchBlockedByMCPReadOnly(method, mutating) is retired and only the table entry is hand-set. The generated scan / scan-detections GETs come out gated natively.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a spec extension the press honors for side-effecting GETs (mark the operation mutating) so the gate, cache bypass and MCP hint follow by construction.

handfixes.summary: tail strips the secret fields (as_uninstall_password, secret_token, custom_headers and the rest of secretFieldKeys) from every polled response before streaming it, and is hidden from the MCP server (mcp:hidden).
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). tail policies and tail notifications streamed every policy's uninstall password and every subscription's signing key and auth headers, while the MCP tail tool advertised readOnlyHint=true and stayed enabled under THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY=1: the twin of the round-2 export finding. As an MCP tool tail also never returned (the MCP argv builder drops follow:false, so the poll loop ran forever). A reprint regenerates tail.go; internal/cli/tail_secrets_test.go fails with the redaction removed.

handfixes.summary: respond pending treats a job search the server did not end with an empty next_cursor (page cap reached, or no cursor confirmation) as incomplete: human output warns and drops the all-clear, and the all-clear itself names what it checked (waiting, timed out, expired, failed; cancelled jobs are not listed). fleet stale applies the same unconfirmed-end rule to its stale and --twins searches, and the respond pending all-clear names any --command / --site filter. parseJobs keeps a job row whose online/data field has an unexpected type and counts any row it still cannot read; respond pending (live and local) and customer report then carry a note instead of an all-clear. fleet sync stores every job row parseJobs can read, and a full sync that could not read or confirm every record marks that resource's last attempt incomplete; fleetHint, respond pending (local) and customer report then name it instead of trusting the older freshness stamp. The same incomplete-sync note reaches fleet stale and fleet health (local), threats spread and threats queue, and customer report for endpoints and detections, and threats queue never suggests a forgotten-isolation restore while the detection or endpoint copy is incomplete.
handfixes.why: Found by the Codex branch review (2026-10-14): view.Truncated reached the JSON output but the table path ignored it, so a scan that hit the page cap could print an all-clear while older failed jobs went unchecked. respond_pending.go is a hand-written novel file; this entry pins the guard against a refactor. Codex round 2 added: a missing next_cursor ended the scan without marking it incomplete, and the old all-clear ('Every job ... completed') counted cancelled jobs as completed. Round 6 found the fleet stale twin (it printed 'No endpoints unseen' after an unconfirmed end) and the filtered all-clear reading as fleet-wide. Codex review round 6 (2026-10-14), P2: a failed job with "online":"true" failed the whole row's decode and vanished, so respond pending printed an all-clear with truncated:false. TestParseJobsNeverDropsSilently. Codex review round 7 (2026-10-14), P2: fleet sync's validJobs still strict-decoded, so the same odd row was dropped at sync time and the earlier freshness stamp let local respond pending print an all-clear. TestFleetSyncNeverLeavesASilentGap. Adversarial review round 11 + Codex round 8 (2026-10-14), P2: the round-7 note covered jobs only; an incomplete detections or endpoints sync still printed an all-clear, and threats queue could suggest a restore over a missed detection. Review round 12 + Codex round 9 (2026-10-14), P2: a first-ever incomplete sync left no marker (UPDATE with no row; now an upsert), the --max-pages note was unreachable behind the !certain case, and an undated detection was dropped by fleet.Queue so it could not block a forgotten-isolation restore. TestRound12SyncAndLoginEdges, TestUndatedDetectionBlocksRestoreSuggestion. Review round 13 + Codex round 10: an undated UNRESOLVED detection was counted but not marked unresolved, so threats queue printed 'Nothing to triage' over it.

handfixes.summary: `golang.org/x/text` is pinned at v0.42.0, above the fixes for GO-2026-5970 and GO-2026-6629
handfixes.why: Press 4.33.5 emits `golang.org/x/text v0.39.0` as an indirect dependency. osv-scanner flags v0.39.0 for GO-2026-6629 (a panic parsing crafted input in x/text/secure/precis). The repo security gate tracks it, and a reprint from a press that still emits v0.39.0 would quietly bring it back. Bumped with `go get golang.org/x/text@v0.41.0` + `go mod tidy`; build and tests pass. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): the 4.35.1 render pins no x/text, so `go mod tidy` resolved v0.14.0; replay_handfixes.py raised it to v0.42.0.

handfixes.summary: `auth status` reports whether THIS process can authenticate: a complete client ID + secret pair (env or saved) counts as authenticated ('minted on first call'), and a cached token bound to a different OAuth client, scope or token URL with no secret to mint a replacement reports authenticated:false, token_bound_elsewhere:true and exits 4 (client.ErrTokenBoundElsewhere), the same verdict doctor gives. Placeholder values and unresolved MCPB ${...} templates never count as a pair (resolveClientCredentials reads the env through cliutil.EnvOverride, like config.Load), and doctor uses the same AuthState, so the two never disagree. Any <...> value is a placeholder (the docs print <client-id>, <your-client-secret>, <value>), auth login reads the env through EnvOverride, and doctor reports a rejected token mint (client.ErrTokenMintRejected) as a credentials ERROR instead of 'API unreachable'. A placeholder that came from THREATDOWN_CLIENT_ID or THREATDOWN_CLIENT_SECRET is reported against that variable, not config.toml, and doctor shows it as a Credentials ERROR with the API not probed. auth login refuses a placeholder client ID or secret (flag or env) before any token request.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review round 8 (2026-10-14): the generated status only checked that a token was cached. With a saved admin login and THREATDOWN_CLIENT_ID=reporting it printed authenticated:true while every API call exited 4; on a fresh home with a valid env ID + secret pair it printed authenticated:false and told the user to export variables that were already exported. An agent gating on `auth status --json` either walked into exit-4 failures or asked the user for credentials they had already given. A reprint regenerates the cached-token-only check. Round 9 (2026-10-14) found the twin: doctor still said 'Auth: not configured' on a fresh home with a valid env pair, and AuthState called placeholder or ${...} values mintable. TestAuthStatusAndDoctorAgreeOnEnvPairs covers all three cases for both commands. Review round 10: the placeholder matcher missed the connector's own documented placeholders, and with a typo'd secret doctor blamed the network. TestDoctorReportsRejectedMintAsCredentials. Adversarial review round 11 (2026-10-14), P2: an env placeholder was reported as 'configured in config.toml' (a file holding no credential) and doctor called it 'API: unreachable'. TestPlaceholderErrorNamesTheEnvVar. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): 4.35.1 masks the token endpoint's error body through maskHeldError, whose maskedError drops the wrapped ErrTokenMintRejected whenever it masks a value, so doctor called a rejected secret 'unreachable' when the body echoed a token. The sentinel now wraps the masked error from outside. TestRejectedMintAndRefreshNeverDeadlock fails on that shape (want ErrTokenMintRejected) and hangs (5 s guard) if the token-state lock is ever taken twice on the rejected mint or refresh path; mint_lock_scan.py flags both paths statically because it cannot see maskHeldError's held=true.

handfixes.summary: `auth set-token` calls cfg.MarkCredentialsExplicit(true, true) before SaveTokens("", "", ...), so it clears the saved client ID and secret even while THREATDOWN_CLIENT_ID is exported. It also saves a zero expiry, since the pasted token's lifetime is unknown.

In the spec it was one endpoint's quarantine list (GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/endpoints/{id}/quarantine) stored under resource_type `endpoints`, the table fleet sync keeps the endpoint mirror in. `sync --resources endpoints` now fails and points at `fleet sync`; the help example names sites,users. `sync --resources` naming endpoints, detections or jobs (endpoint_jobs) is refused as a usage error before --full resets any sync state. `jobs` (fleet sync's own name for endpoint_jobs) is refused too. The MCP context tool no longer marks endpoints syncable, and the MCP store next_step and doctor's cache hints name fleet sync for endpoints, detections and jobs. The missing-store, open-error and no-rows MCP messages and the context guidance name fleet sync too.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review round 11 (2026-10-14), P2: `sync --resources endpoints --full --path-context account_id=a1 --path-context id=m01` reconciled away every real endpoint, stored a quarantine row in their place and re-stamped the copy complete, so fleet stale --data-source local listed the quarantine row as an endpoint. sync.go is generated (DO NOT EDIT); a reprint re-emits the resource from the spec unless x-resource handling drops it. TestGenericSyncLeavesTheEndpointMirrorAlone. Review round 12 (2026-10-14), P2: the --full reset loop zero-stamped the fleet-owned sync_state rows before the name was rejected, clearing the incomplete marker, and the pointer only showed with --human-friendly. Review round 13 + Codex round 10 (2026-10-14), P2: MCP next_step sent agents to generic sync, which can never complete a fleet-owned resource; context advertised endpoints as syncable; `sync --resources jobs --full` wrote a junk sync_state row. Review round 14 + Codex round 11: those messages still sent agents to generic sync only, and four of the new strings were not pinned. TestStoreHintsNameFleetSync.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Drop the quarantine path from the spec's sync resources (or give it its own resource name) so a reprint does not re-emit it under `endpoints`.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 3 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: cases action (POST /v1/casemgmt/accounts/{account_id}/cases/action); endpoint-jobs bulk-issue (POST /v1/jobs/bulk); suspicious-activity close (POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/sa/close).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token or changes stored credentials: neither the client's automatic client-credentials mint nor `auth login --dry-run` sends the client secret to the token URL, and `auth set-token --dry-run` and `auth logout --dry-run` neither save nor clear anything
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py write-safety found every --dry-run of a write command putting one request on the wire: authHeader ran before the dry-run branch and, with no cached token, POSTed the client ID and secret to the token URL and cached the token, while the generated comment and the docs say a dry run sends nothing. `auth login` minted through its own path and ignored --dry-run, and `auth set-token` and `auth logout` saved and cleared credentials under --dry-run (found by Codex review round 1). Same fix shape as connectwise-rmm, sophos-central and watchguard (dry-run-never-mints). TestDryRunNeverMintsAToken, TestAuthLoginDryRunSendsNothing and TestAuthSetTokenAndLogoutHonorDryRun count requests to a stub token server (each with a live control that proves the probe reaches the mint) and fail on the generated code.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: client.go.tmpl should skip the client-credentials mint when DryRun is set (the dry-run preview already uses cached material only), and auth.go.tmpl's login should honor the root --dry-run flag.

handfixes.summary: The two derive-lock tests (ContendedAppendIsDerivedBeforeReturn, CaughtUpPassDoesNotWait) wait on what the pass is doing, read from goroutine stacks, instead of fixed 200 ms, 500 ms and 5 s windows; every remaining wait is bounded by the test binary's own deadline
handfixes.why: On windows(fortinet) in CI (2026-10-22, PR #421) the contended test failed with 'contended pass did not finish after the peer released the lock': after release the pass opens a fresh SQLite store and commits, and a slow Windows runner took longer than the fixed 5 s. The 200 ms 'did not return while held' window was also weak: on a slow runner it could elapse before the pass even reached the wait. The contended test now waits until the pass is provably blocked in cliutil.WithFileLock called from DeriveFlagCorrections (it cannot return before release), so it is stronger, not weaker. Proven: a pass that returns early under contention fails it; a caught-up pass that polls or blocks fails the caught-up test; with a simulated 6 s store open after the lock, the old test fails with the CI message and the new one passes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated internal/learn derive_test.go should use this state-based wait in place of the fixed windows.

handfixes.summary: The token client's same-origin check compares hosts the way the network resolves them: an IP literal by address with an exact IPv6 zone, a DNS name ASCII case-insensitively, a non-ASCII name exactly
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). Press 4.33.5 already sends every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, but its oauthTokenSameOrigin compared hostnames with strings.EqualFold, which also folds IPv6 zone names (fe80::1%LAN0 passed for fe80::1%lan0, two different peers when the interfaces differ) and Unicode case. It now compares an IP literal exactly as a netip.Addr (zone included) and folds ASCII case only for DNS names. TestOAuthTokenSameOriginComparesHostsLikeTheNetwork failed on the previous commit and passes now; TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin pins the login path.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

TestPartialSiteResponseKeepsTheAccount and TestFleetSyncNeverDeletesOnACachedSiteList fail on that cut.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, client-credentials mint and auth login, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand, terminal checks through credkit.Terminal, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. The credential store, config.toml (and its legacy copy and snapshot restore) and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own layer. Classes closed, each by a test in cli/internal/credwire/leak_test.go seen failing first on the pre-kit build: a token-endpoint error body that echoes the client secret, printed by auth login whole and by the automatic mint in part (TestTokenEndpointEchoOfClientSecretIsWithheld, CLI and MCP); an API error that echoes part of the minted bearer (TestAPIErrorEchoOfMintedTokenIsWithheld, CLI, --agent and MCP), and the same piece HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded, base64 or hex, with the 0.1.3 promise for the whole token kept (TestEncodedEchoOfMintedTokenIsWithheld); every startup source held before the first byte of output, the client pair, THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, SPACEFAST_TOKEN, a base URL password, the credential store, config.toml, a malformed config and a profile value under a credential flag's name (TestStartupCredentialsHeldBeforeAnyOutput); a held credential refused to another origin and over plain http, the --deliver webhook, an off-origin token URL and a plain http API (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP); a --stdin request body held before a --dry-run preview (TestStdinBodyHeldBeforePreview); and the learn journal, written with credkit.AppendFile, never records a held credential (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential). Two missing-data guards, each seen failing on a mutated build: `feedback --stdin` keeps its body (TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded; --stdin is a StdinFlags name, so the kit held the feedback text whole and withheld the local record; compactStdinBody takes a feedback command line's body off stdin before the kit reads it and RestoreFeedbackStdin hands it back), and ordinary results still print and cache (TestOrdinaryOutputStillPrints, failing with an over-broad ResponseFields). In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the test seams swap. The vendor's own secret response fields (as_uninstall_password, secret_token, custom_headers) are not declared: their reads are Credential tier (secret-reads-credential-tier) and declaring them would withhold the reads that return them.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
